scope: Language-family history and publication taxonomy, supported by retained primary-source review and runtime observations. Actual runtime identity is joined separately to the prepared qualification admission.

metadata.label: Rebol 3
metadata.note: Rebol 3 interprets user-defined functions with dynamic value types, first-class functions, prototype objects and automatic tracing garbage collection. These categories describe the language/runtime model; foreign-library allocation is excluded.

release.release_note: Family introduction year: the October 1, 1998 Core 1.0 announcement reports alpha and beta releases during the preceding ten months, placing their start in late 1997. The designer also dates the V0 prototype to 1997. Core 1.0 itself was released in 1998; this date is not the release date of the measured Oldes Rebol 3 runtime.

primary_sources.supports: Core 1.0 announcement dated October 1, 1998; preceding ten months of alpha and beta releases. Late-1997 introduction is an explicit inference.
Designer timeline identifies a 1997 V0 prototype. Used only to corroborate the early family year; later-version timeline is not substituted for the contemporary 1.0 announcement.
User-defined function values are interpreted; datatype constraints on arguments are optional. The error/assert example rebinds one word from an integer to a string.
Function and closure values support higher-order programming; documentation includes a closure-producing function.
Sequential assignment, conditional and iteration examples support imperative classification; functions are values.
Objects contain state and functions; existing objects serve as prototypes for copied and extended objects.
Automatic garbage collection is the normal language runtime facility; explicit recycle is optional.
Official Oldes runtime release identity 3.22.1, separate from the family introduction date; this web page does not verify the installed binary.

local_source_read.supports: Retained source implements tracing mark and sweep, matching the existing gc taxonomy. This inspection does not establish binary/source equivalence.

scope_limits: The 1997 date describes the Rebol language family; Core 1.0 was announced in 1998. It is not the release year of the selected Oldes runtime.
The selected runtime reports Rebol/Bulk 3.22.1. Its displayed build timestamp is not treated as a historical language release date.
The retained feature probe observed interpreted function values, dynamic rebinding and automatic collection in that probe only.
Retained collector source supports the tracing-GC classification without proving binary/source equivalence or a numeric GC configuration.
